newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey may readjust oil imports for Iraqi purchase.
newsitem.headline: Turkey may readjust oil imports for Iraqi purchase.

text.p: Turkey's state oil refinery Tupras may readjust its annual oil import contracts for 1997 to make room for crude purchases from Iraq under a U.N.-monitored scheme, officials said.
"There is a study which considers readjusting this year's oil imports from other countries," said an official.
"The readjustment may be made either on imports from one country or it can be spread over contracts with several countries," he told Reuters.

Tupras was the first company whose contract to buy 75,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude was approved by the United Nations, which in December allowed Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to buy food and medicines.
"Tupras' oil import contracts are made on a minimum and maximum amount basis. The adjustment can be made over the minimum limit with one country or more," the official said.

He said a readjustment of Turkey's contract with Saudi Arabia, its main supplier, for purchases of a minimum 8.5 million tonnes annually and a maximum of 10.5 million tonnes, could be one of the options being considered. He did not give any other details.
Turkey and Iran agreed last month to renew a contract under which Turkey imports 4-4.5 million tonnes of Iranian crude annually.
